stem: In the Business Disability Forum's Accessibility Maturity Model, what characterizes Level 1 (Informal)?

options.text: Accessibility activities are reactive and driven by isolated champions without centralized strategy or organizational coordination.
options.shortLabel: Reactive efforts led by isolated champions
options.rationale: In Level 1 (Informal), there is no centralized strategy, governance, or documented policy; accessibility relies entirely on the ad hoc goodwill of isolated individuals reacting to immediate issues.

options.text: Accessibility performance is measured through formal KPIs, periodic audits, and management review cycles across the business units.
options.rationale: Managing accessibility through quantitative metrics, formal performance targets, and regular operational audits defines Level 4 (Managed).

options.text: Accessibility policies and technical standards are documented, but adoption varies between business units and regions.
options.rationale: Formally documenting policies and standards while implementation remains patchy or siloed is the defining characteristic of Level 2 (Defined).

options.text: Accessibility practices and training are built into regular development, procurement, and content workflows.
options.rationale: Embedding consistent, repeatable processes, training, and tools across regular business operations characterizes Level 3 (Repeatable).

explanation: The Business Disability Forum's Accessibility Maturity Model benchmarks an organization's maturity across five levels: Level 1 (Informal - ad hoc, reactive actions by isolated individuals without enterprise strategy), Level 2 (Defined - policies and standards are documented but applied unevenly), Level 3 (Repeatable - processes are embedded predictably into workflows), Level 4 (Managed - quantitative KPIs and audits are tracked as standard business operations), and Level 5 (Best practice - continuous innovation and industry leadership).

references.title: Business Disability Forum: Accessibility Maturity Model
